title: Why this sheriff's race matters | Letters To Editor | ellsworthamerican.com
text:
To the Editor:
As a registered Democrat, I believe in my party’s values. But choosing our sheriff should be about character, integrity and experience—not party affiliation.
I have known Corey Bagley for years and have seen him as a coach, mentor, law enforcement officer, father, husband and community supporter. Through these roles, I have come to know someone I consider hardworking, honest, trustworthy and committed to others.
Having served in county government for six years, I have witnessed changes within our county. Over the past three years, under the current Sheriff’s Office administration, I have noticed declining morale, less participation in county events and a noticeably different atmosphere surrounding the Sheriff’s Office.
Just this week, we celebrated the retirement of a county employee who dedicated 39 years to Hancock County. Yet, to my knowledge, no one from the Sheriff’s Office stopped by to wish her well. This may seem small, but recognizing decades of service demonstrates respect and appreciation. These gestures strengthen the relationships that hold a workplace and community together. When they are missing, it raises questions about our workplace culture and sense of connection.
A sheriff must cross party lines, put the community first and serve everyone fairly. Public safety is not partisan, and leadership should never be about party loyalty alone.
I question whether the Democratic candidate reflects the core values I associate with my party. When a candidate’s actions or positions appear inconsistent with those principles, it raises questions about the authenticity of their party affiliation and campaign.
Being a Democrat does not mean automatically supporting the Democratic candidate. It means making a choice based on my values, experience, and judgment.
For me, this election is about character over party, integrity over labels and choosing the person I believe can best serve Hancock County.
Lori Whitney
Surry
